test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-6) Official paper (Held On: 9 May 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A person covers a certain distance at a certain speed. If he increases his speed by 30%, then he takes 15 minutes less to cover the same distance. Find the time taken by him to cover the distance when travelling at his original speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed Ratio** (Original : New) = 100 : 130 = 10 : 13

Since **Distance** is constant, **Time Ratio** = 13 : 10

Difference in time = 13 − 10 = 3 units

According to the question, 3 units = 15 min ⇒ 1 unit = 5 min

Original Time = 13 units = 13 × 5 = 65 min = 1 hr 05 min

**∴ The correct answer is 1 hr 05 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed increase = 30%

Time reduction = 15 min

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time (D = S × T)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe624782055c2b4458ed08bbe6cc3413cf0f6a48b35ce8eefc0f9344759239fa.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original speed be S and original time be T.

⇒ New speed = S + 30% of S = 1.3S

⇒ New time = T − 15 min

⇒ Since distance is the same: S × T = 1.3S × (T − 15)

⇒ T = 1.3T − 19.5

⇒ 1.3T − T = 19.5

⇒ 0.3T = 19.5

⇒ T = 19.5 ÷ 0.3 = 65 min

⇒ 65 min = 1 hr 05 min

**∴ The correct answer is 1 hr 05 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion Rule

When **Distance** is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Average Speed

If a person covers the same distance at speed x and speed y, the **Average Speed** is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p
